title: Cisco Certified Network Associate (CCNA) v1.1
note: Exam topic text is Cisco's; it is reproduced here only as the tag map. Item text in packs/ccna/ is original. v2.0 replaces v1.1 on Feb 3, 2027 (PLAN.md §1). obj ids: the topic number ("3.4") or a sub-topic ("3.4.c") — the validator accepts either; the first digit is the domain.

format.passScore: not published by Cisco (varies per exam form; see dev/specs/ccna.md §1)

1.1.t: Explain the role and function of network components

1.2.t: Describe characteristics of network topology architectures

1.3.t: Compare physical interface and cabling types

1.4.t: Identify interface and cable issues (collisions, errors, mismatch duplex, and/or speed)

1.6.t: Configure and verify IPv4 addressing and subnetting

1.8.t: Configure and verify IPv6 addressing and prefix

sub.a: Unicast (global, unique local, and link local)

1.10.t: Verify IP parameters for Client OS (Windows, Mac OS, Linux)

1.12.t: Explain virtualization fundamentals (server virtualization, containers, and VRFs)

2.1.t: Configure and verify VLANs (normal range) spanning multiple switches

2.3.t: Configure and verify Layer 2 discovery protocols (Cisco Discovery Protocol and LLDP)

2.5.t: Interpret basic operations of Rapid PVST+ Spanning Tree Protocol

sub.a: Root port, root bridge (primary/secondary), and other port names
sub.d: Root guard, loop guard, BPDU filter, and BPDU guard

2.6.t: Describe Cisco Wireless Architectures and AP modes

2.7.t: Describe physical infrastructure connections of WLAN components (AP, WLC, access/trunk ports, and LAG)

2.8.t: Describe network device management access (Telnet, SSH, HTTP, HTTPS, console, TACACS+/RADIUS, and cloud managed)

2.9.t: Interpret the wireless LAN GUI configuration for client connectivity, such as WLAN creation, security settings, QoS profiles, and advanced settings

3.1.t: Interpret the components of routing table

3.2.t: Determine how a router makes a forwarding decision by default

3.3.t: Configure and verify IPv4 and IPv6 static routing

3.4.t: Configure and verify single area OSPFv2

3.5.t: Describe the purpose, functions, and concepts of first hop redundancy protocols

4.1.t: Configure and verify inside source NAT using static and pools

4.2.t: Configure and verify NTP operating in a client and server mode

4.3.t: Explain the role of DHCP and DNS within the network

4.4.t: Explain the function of SNMP in network operations

4.5.t: Describe the use of syslog features, including facilities and severity levels

4.6.t: Configure and verify DHCP client and relay

4.7.t: Explain the forwarding per-hop behavior (PHB) for QoS such as classification, marking, queuing, congestion, policing, and shaping

4.8.t: Configure network devices for remote access using SSH

4.9.t: Describe the capabilities and functions of TFTP/FTP in the network

5.1.t: Define key security concepts (threats, vulnerabilities, exploits, and mitigation techniques)

5.2.t: Describe security program elements (user awareness, training, and physical access control)

5.3.t: Configure and verify device access control using local passwords

5.4.t: Describe security password policy elements, such as management, complexity, and password alternatives (multifactor authentication, certificates, and biometrics)

5.5.t: Describe IPsec remote access and site-to-site VPNs

5.6.t: Configure and verify access control lists

5.7.t: Configure and verify Layer 2 security features (DHCP snooping, dynamic ARP inspection, and port security)

5.8.t: Compare authentication, authorization, and accounting concepts

5.9.t: Describe wireless security protocols (WPA, WPA2, and WPA3)

5.10.t: Configure and verify WLAN within the GUI using WPA2 PSK

6.1.t: Explain how automation impacts network management

6.2.t: Compare traditional networks with controller-based networking

6.3.t: Describe controller-based, software defined architecture (overlay, underlay, and fabric)

sub.a: Separation of control plane and data plane

6.4.t: Explain AI (generative and predictive) and machine learning in network operations

6.5.t: Describe characteristics of REST-based APIs (authentication types, CRUD, HTTP verbs, and data encoding)

6.6.t: Recognize the capabilities of configuration management mechanisms such as Ansible and Terraform
